teaser: A BBC live page at breakfast became an evidence vault, a section and a dedicated site by lunchtime: capture first, because a breaking story's pages change by the hour.
core_idea: When a story is still breaking, the first thing to build is the vault that captures the evidence, dated and hashed, before the pages change, and the pages, the section and the dedicated site are then readers of that vault, with what went wrong kept in the record too.

nodes.label: The BBC live page
nodes.summary: Opened at 06:16 UTC on 22 October; a new post appeared between the first two copies.

nodes.label: Numbers that did not add up
nodes.summary: 70% of the internet beside 30 million websites, and agencies saying take sites offline.

nodes.label: Capture before you write
nodes.summary: Live pages, down pages and posts change within hours, so the evidence is kept before the article is written.

nodes.label: The evidence vault
nodes.summary: A private sgit vault created at 08:03, holding 184 sources and 177 captures by 12:05.

nodes.label: The capture tool
nodes.summary: Raw page, rendered page, text, screenshot and headers, each hashed in a provenance file.

nodes.label: Captures are only added
nodes.summary: A page captured many times leaves a dated series that records how the story moved.

nodes.label: One file per writer
nodes.summary: A row per source and claims and timeline files per agent, so several agents write at once.

nodes.label: The /php-flaws/ section
nodes.summary: Pushed at 08:13 with what is known, what is not, the timeline and the claims by status.

nodes.label: NCSC-NL's inventory, bundled
nodes.summary: The whole repository kept as a git bundle; 674 products counted at commit cca173c64ec5.

nodes.label: Numbers pinned to measures
nodes.summary: 70% of websites, 2.6 million hosts, about 6,000 resources in Latvia: different things measured.

nodes.label: Agencies disagree on offline
nodes.summary: The NSA and CISA say take systems offline; the NCSC-NL does not advise it.

nodes.label: Forty sources nearly lost
nodes.summary: Two agents stopped before committing; the lead agent recovered their captures hours later.

nodes.label: A site of its own
nodes.summary: php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai reads the same vault, facts only, with briefings per role.

nodes.label: Retire the section
nodes.summary: The section moves to the dedicated site and leaves a pointer; the newsroom keeps context and opinion.

quotes.text: A finished article can wait; the evidence for it cannot.
quotes.why: The argument of the article in one line: why the vault came before the page.

quotes.text: A count like 674 is only useful with the commit it was counted at, because the next pull request changes it.
quotes.why: Provenance for a number, stated as a working rule.

figures.caption: The morning of 22 October 2026 in two lanes, in UTC from 06:00 to 12:15. The top lane is the story as its sources date it: the BBC live page opening at 06:16, the NSA's advice reported at 06:56, the researcher on Radio 4 at 07:00, two French prefecture sites on maintenance pages at 08:19, and the NCSC-NL inventory at 674 products at 08:41. The bottom lane is the newsroom: the first copy of the BBC page at 07:55, the vault at 08:03, the first complete capture at 08:06, the section here at 08:13, the dedicated site's first release at 09:27, and the vault at 184 sources by 12:05.

Who wrote the 184 sources in the evidence vault by 12:05 UTC, and what reads it. On the left, six writers with their counts: the dedicated site's agent 83, the government collector 37, the news collector 31, the primary-sources collector 17, the researchers' collector 14 and the lead agent 2. In the middle, the vault: 184 sources, 177 dated captures, 855 files hashed at capture, 128 claims and events in per-agent files. On the right, what reads it: this newsroom's section, the dedicated site, and, still to come, articles here and anyone the vault is opened to.
